_label: Fun facts, all from cited Wikipedia articles (accessed 2026-10-11). Uniform numbers for retired players are from Wikipedia's List of Major League Baseball retired numbers.

timeline: Founded as the Chicago White Stockings.
National League charter franchise - one of two remaining from the NL's first season.
The Chicago Daily News calls the young team the 'Cubs' (1902); name adopted officially five years later.
116-36 (.763), the modern-era record winning percentage - then lost the World Series to the crosstown White Sox.
Back-to-back World Series titles; first team to play in three straight World Series and first to win two.
'Baseball's Sad Lexicon' immortalizes Tinker to Evers to Chance.
First Cubs game at what is now Wrigley Field (April 20): 7-6 over the Reds in 11 innings.
William Wrigley Jr. acquires the club.
Pennant, then a World Series loss to Detroit - the 'Curse of the Billy Goat' year.
The 'Fall of '69'.
Lights installed at Wrigley Field.
'Five more outs' from the World Series.
103 wins; beat Cleveland after trailing the World Series 3 games to 1, ending a 108-year title drought. The parade drew ~5 million.
Theo Epstein resigns as president (Nov 17); Jed Hoyer succeeds him.
Carter Hawkins hired as general manager.
history.rivalry: Cardinals (the I-55 Series; Cubs lead 1,253-1,196 through Oct 2021), Brewers (the I-94 rivalry; 2018 Game 163 went to Milwaukee) and the crosstown White Sox (1906 World Series; White Sox lead the regular-season series 72-64). Retired-number flags fly from the Wrigley foul poles.

timeline: Early years
'Standing cub' logo, a primitive 'C-UBS' mark, a 'wishbone C' (later adopted by the Bears); navy blue and sometimes red until the mid-1940s, then royal blue and red.
First version of today's pinstriped home uniform.
All-blue cap with red 'C' outlined in white first worn - still the main cap.
Cub-head sleeve patch added.
Switch to pullovers.
Powder-blue road uniforms; pinstripes added 1978, names 1979.
Blue road tops with plain white pants.
Back to buttoned gray road uniforms.
Blue alternate returns; 'cute cub' patch.
Current road grays (radial 'Chicago') and blue alternate; 'walking cub' sleeve patch.
'Wrigleyville' City Connect: navy with light blue, marquee-inspired wordmark, Chicago-flag star on the cap (worn until 2024).
First uniform sponsor: Motorola Mobility.
Powder-blue home alternate inspired by Chicago blues music, with a guitar-pick city logo; worn for summer Friday day games.

facts: April 23, 1914 as Weeghman Park for the Federal League's Chicago Whales; Cubs Park 1920-26; Wrigley Field since 1927.
Oldest park in the National League and second-oldest in MLB after Fenway (1912); the only remaining Federal League park.
Planted in 1937 at Bill Veeck's suggestion; now Boston ivy, which survives Chicago winters. It turns red in autumn.
Hand-turned, installed 1937; the clock (added 1941) has never lost time.
Red art-deco marquee over the main entrance, installed 1934 (originally green), painted red in 1960.
Last MLB park to add lights, in 1988; night games are still limited by agreement with the city.
A 'W' or 'L' flag flies from the scoreboard after every game - a tradition since the 1937 rebuild.
Lake Michigan is under a mile away: spring winds blow in, summer winds can blow out - one of MLB's most unpredictable parks.
Fans watch from rooftops on Waveland and Sheffield beyond the outfield.
'The Friendly Confines', popularized by Ernie Banks. Address: 1060 W. Addison St.
